The bottles are now opaque milky white rather than clear glass, the fridge labels are saturated cobalt, and the tumblers are opaque white cups where the render shows small clear glasses. The brewer bay is right. The real door is also a wide dark frame with a lens-shaped bulge round an oval latch, not a round knob on a thin stile. The monitor still stands proud. issues.detail: Door-2 welcome glass cabinet (m03, m16, m14)
issues.problem: With no pane and emissive contents (e 0.1 back wall, e 0.08 shelves, e 0.04 boxes), the cabinet reads as an open self-lit shelf. The interior is brighter and more contrasty than the photo, there is no glass cue at all, and from the J aisle (m14) it is a pale taupe box punched into the dark tower. In omaat_room_32 the pane is smoked: contents are visible but sit about 0.5-0.7x darker than in the render, with one broad soft reflection near the top and the dark frame reading as a door. The door frame is also different. The real top rail is about 0.12 m deep and carries the white caution text, the stiles are about 0.06 m, and the latch is an oval thumb-latch in a lens-shaped bulge of the left stile at mid height. The render has a thin frame and a round knob that overhangs the stile. The hinge-side reflection line reads as a rod (m16 x~830).
issues.fix: In buildWelcomeGalley (10_mono.js ~l.369-381): (1) Drop the emissives: back wall { c: '#3a3633', r: 0.6 }, with no e; shelves e 0 and c '#6a665f'; boxes scaled to ~0.7x (#77746f->#55524e, #938f88->#67645f, #a8a49c->#7a766f) with no e; tray e 0.02. (2) Add a glass cue that is not opaque and not upright. Use one soft gQuad(0.30, 0.22) reflection in the upper third, rotated ~0.35 rad about z, at o+0.0905 in { c: '#4a4744', r: 0.05, m: 0.4 }, and a second, narrower one lower down. Delete the 0.006 hinge-side strip. (3) Frame: top rail gBox(0.44, 0.12, 0.03) at y 1.78 with the caution plate moved onto it, and stiles 0.06 wide. Replace the round boss with gRBox(0.08, 0.14, 0.02, 0.04, 2) in welcomeChar on the left stile (lens bulge), with a gRBox(0.035, 0.06, 0.012, 0.017, 2) MONMAT.latch oval on it. Check m14 from the aisle: the cabinet should read darker than the tower's light grey recess.

issues.problem: After the lighting changes the wall reads as near-uniform off-white. The cloud strata exist, but their amplitude (inkGround #dddbd0 to inkCloud at t<=1 after the ^1.3 and lowY<1 attenuation) is too low to survive the brighter exposure. The photo's grey-blue cloud bands span almost 3x the tonal range, and the wall is the hero view from every Suite.
issues.evidence: m02 region x 640-900 y 200-300: mean #d0d1ce, p5 #c1c3be, p95 #d8d8d5 (spread ~23). w10 same region: p5 #9fa49e, p95 #d4d4d1 (spread ~53). omaatF_2 x 660-1060 y 170-310: mean #bdb8ae, p5 #8e8a84, p95 #d3cec2 (spread ~69).
issues.fix: In inkWall (10_mono.js ~l.686): widen the band and lift the depth. Use t = clamp((n - 0.36) / 0.22, 0, 1) ** 1.1 * lowY with lowY = clamp(1.25 - 0.4 * y / H, 0.65, 1), and darken MONMAT.inkCloud by about 20 % (target cloud core ~#8a8a84 after lighting). Optionally drop inkGround to '#d4d1c6' so the photo's mean of ~#bdb8ae is reached in this exposure. If the lighting owner settles the F exposure lower, re-check the spread before committing.

issues.detail: Brewer jug and head (m09, m01, m12, q19, m03)
issues.problem: The jug is a uniform matte mid-grey with a hard white stick highlight. The dark reflection band plus the handle read as a black ']' glyph, so it looks like a frosted plastic bottle with a sticker. sansY_44's jugs are mirror stainless with broad soft dark and bright bands that follow the curvature. The head carries a large black 'window', which reads as a microwave. The real brewer head is a plain satin band with a label and the brew handle.
issues.fix: brewer() l.189: remove the ovenGlass window, or shrink it to gQuad(uW*0.5, 0.012) as a label strip in MONMAT.label. l.198-199: replace the two flat quads with vertex-colour banding on the lathe. After B.add(gLathe(...)), loop the new vertices and set the colour from the azimuth: c = lerp('#2a2926', '#d8d6d0', 0.5+0.5*cos(3*atan2(x, z) + 0.6)). That gives two dark and two bright vertical bands that wrap round the belly. Set MONMAT.jug r to 0.12.

issues.detail: Door-3 bar bottles and tumblers (m05, m06, q11)
issues.problem: The bottles are now opaque milky white-grey with bright labels (bottleClear #b4c2c5 + e 0.02). The clear glass in samchui_render_11 reads dark, with the black back panel showing through, plus bright edge highlights and a white label band. The fridge bottles have saturated cobalt bands, where the render has muted, full-height blue water. The tumblers are opaque white cups, where the render shows small clear, dark glasses.
issues.fix: MONMAT.bottleClear { c: '#4b5458', r: 0.04, m: 0.5 } with no e. Keep the white label band in bottle(). Add a 0.004-wide bright gQuad edge highlight '#d8dee0' on one side of each body. bottleBlue { c: '#3d4f8a', r: 0.3 }, covering the lower 70 % of the fridge bottles rather than a band. MONMAT.tumbler { c: '#3c4043', r: 0.04, m: 0.5 } and h 0.05 with an r 0.03 lathe.

issues.problem: The door is ebony to the edges inside a thin light frame. tpa_Image-2-3 shows a wide (~0.06 m) satin-aluminium frame round the whole door and a plain aluminium kick panel about 0.2 m tall above the chevron strip. The lock boss is also small and flat.
issues.evidence: m19 door (490,350) #282122, frame ~3 px. tpa_Image-2-3 frame (240,300) #e2e3e5, lock boss (380,305) #a9afaf on a curved plate ~0.12 m tall.
